messages:
elena: noticing a sustained throughput sag on prod-gpu-1 since ~08:10 UTC, p95 latency doubled and a few 503s. Worker restarts are correlating with the spikes. anyone watching?

tyler: yep seeing it on the dashboard. replicas 3->1 for some workers around 08:12, then flapping restarts.

jasper: infra-bot reported OOMs: "Runtime worker exited(code=137)" and CUDA OOM logs in syslogs. attaching snippets below:
```
[08:11:43] runtime-worker[pid=7421]: CUDA ERROR: out of memory when allocating 2.3 GiB
[08:11:43] runtime-worker[pid=7421]: terminating with signal 9
[08:11:44] kubelet: container runtime-worker restarted (OOMKilled)
```

kevin: I pulled a pmap from the restarted process — heap shows large free but fragmented regions, high number of small allocations in slab allocator. Looks like KV cache churn increased.

elena: what changed recently? any kernel-selection or batching PRs?

tyler: PR #482 (batching heuristics) rolled on canary yesterday. It increases dynamic batch target for seq_len<=512 when latency headroom exists.

jasper: profiling from 08:05-08:15 attached: increased average batch size from 2.1 -> 4.7 then a spike to 12 for a short window. KV cache hit rate dropped from 92% -> 64% during spike. When batch size spikes, sequential requests evict KV entries and cause re-materialization cost.

kevin: nvprof snippet shows fallback to generic attention kernel for many calls (fallback rate ~18%). That fallback path allocates transient buffers more aggressively than the optimized kernel which assumes reuse. So fragmentation + bigger temporary allocations -> OOM.

ops_sre: infra-bot: Deploy 2045-rc3 rolled to prod-gpu-1 at 07:58 UTC (changes: batching-heuristic v2, kernel-selection heuristic tweak).

elena: hypothesis: batching heuristic increases batch sizes in mixed seq workloads, causing more KV churn and temporary allocations -> allocator fragmentation -> worker OOM -> restarts -> throughput drop. Also kernel-selection fallback increases transient allocation pressure.

tyler: quick mitigation ideas: revert batching v2 on prod, force-fallback off for specific model (pin kernel to optimized path), and reduce max batching window. Which do we want asap?

jasper: we can hotfix by setting env RUNTIME_MAX_BATCH_MS=8 (was 25) and KERNEL_FORCE_PIN=optimized for the affected model. That avoids huge batches and forces the efficient kernel. Minimal service interruption (just config reloads).

kevin: also enabling allocator compaction sweep will help (ALLOC_COMPACT=true). It trades a tiny CPU cost for lower fragmentation.

elena: assign: jasper do the config roll (max_batch + kernel pin), kevin enable compaction, tyler prepare rollback PR for batching v2 (PR #482 revert). I'll coordinate postmortem and notify customers if needed.

jasper: rolling configs to prod-gpu-1 now. running: `kubectl set env deploy/runtime-worker RUNTIME_MAX_BATCH_MS=8 KERNEL_FORCE_PIN=optimized -n prod`

[08:27] infra-bot: configmap updated, deployments restarted (gradual).

kevin: enabling allocator compaction on prod-gpu-1. patching helm values and restarting one node at a time.

[08:45] jasper: initial smoke: p95 back down ~20%, batch sizes stabilized at 2-3, KV hit rate up to 89%. no new OOMs in the last 12m on pod set.

tyler: rolling back PR #482 queued if we see reoccur.

elena: next steps: full heap/profiler capture from one affected pod for offline analysis, add a regression test for mixed-seq workloads hitting batching heuristic, and add an alert for KV hit-rate drop >15% relative to baseline. assigning owners in the postmortem doc.

kevin: adding note: watch for kernel-selection heuristic to incorrectly pick generic kernel when sequence length distribution is multimodal — need to add a hysteresis/check to prevent oscillation.

elena: thanks all. I'll file incident postmortem and link metrics + traces. :thumbsup:
